description: JSONPath query evaluator returns dictionary keys instead of values when evaluating wildcard `*` selectors on nested objects, and fails on negative array indices.
spec_notes: Invariant: Object wildcard selector `*` on a dictionary must extract the list of its values, preserving item content.

import re
from typing import List
from tokens import PathSegment

def parse_path(path_expr: str) -> List[PathSegment]:
    segments = []
    raw_parts = path_expr.strip("$.").split(".")
    for part in raw_parts:
        if part == "*":
            segments.append(PathSegment(key="*", is_wildcard=True))
            continue
        match = re.match(r"^(\w+)(?:\[(-?\d+)\])?$", part)
        if match:
            key = match.group(1)
            idx = int(match.group(2)) if match.group(2) is not None else None
            segments.append(PathSegment(key=key, index=idx))
        else:
            segments.append(PathSegment(key=part))
    return segments
